I am an undergraduate in Building Engineering and Construction Management at
RUET. My work sits where structural design meets the construction site: I model and
analyse reinforced-concrete buildings in ETABS, draft and design in AutoCAD, Revit
and SketchUp, and have inspected reinforcement on site in Rajshahi. My research
looks at geopolymer concrete made with recycled concrete fines, a route to lower-
carbon construction in Bangladesh.

Microstructural Performance of Recycled Concrete Fine Aggregate as Geopolymer
Concrete

Supervisor:
Aojoy Kumar Shuvo, Assistant Professor, Dept. of BECM, RUET

Investigates how recycled concrete fine aggregate, recovered from demolished concrete, changes the microstructure and
performance of geopolymer concrete, a cement-free binder made by activating industrial by-products with an alkaline
solution.

Microstructural Properties of Geopolymer Concrete: A Comprehensive Review

A synthesis of 55 studies (1991–2026) on how precursors and alkaline activators shape the gel, pore structure, interfacial
transition zone and microcracking of geopolymer binders. The central finding: the soluble silicate supplied by the
activator and the calcium available in the binder, more than hydroxide molarity, decide whether a porous N-A-S-H gel
or a space-filling C-(N)-A-S-H gel forms. Every activator variable has a system-specific optimum beyond which
porosity, microcracking and efflorescence increase.

Chain of influence from the activator variables to the hardened microstructure, as indicated
by the reviewed studies.

Change in 28-day strength with replacement level for six
recycled materials, compiled from the literature. Directly
relevant to the thesis.

Six-Storey Residential Building

Stories:
6
Floor area:
1,200 sq ft per floor

Context:

A regular reinforced-concrete moment-resisting frame, modelled in
3D with beams, columns and floor slabs on a fixed base. The staircase
is modelled as inclined slabs from floor to floor, so its weight and
stiffness are part of the analysis. Because the stair sits off-centre, it can
introduce torsion in a small building.

3D ETABS model of a wide, low RC frame of about five bays in each direction, with the stair and lift room on the roof.

across many bays, and the difference in axial load between interior, edge and corner columns

Twisted Diagrid High-Rise

Left: the finished model. Right: held to show its scale.

Diagrid exoskeleton.
Strips spiral up in both directions
and cross to form a diagonal grid. In real towers this
perimeter system carries both gravity and lateral loads, so
fewer vertical columns are needed.

Rotated floor plates.
Each slab turns slightly from the
one below, creating the twist. The slabs act as diaphragms
that tie the outer frame to the core.

Central core.
A square shaft stands in for the lift and stair
core. With the diagrid it forms a tube-in-tube lateral system.

Tapered crown.
The tower narrows toward the top, reducing
wind load where the bending lever arm is longest.

Interior Design of an Office Building

Area:
2,668 sq ft
Supervisor:
Md. Towfik Hassan, Lecturer, BECM

Team:
5 members

SketchUp plan

AutoCAD plan

Zoning: private, semi-
private, public

Reception

Conference room

Open workstations

Palette

A modern-minimalist office with a Scandinavian palette set in proportions: 50–55% neutral whites and greys, 30–35% oak,
10–15% black accents and under 5% warm brown. The plan is zoned from public (reception) through semi-private
(workstations, breakout area) to private (CEO room, cabins), and includes a nursing room beside the women’s washroom.

Colour Scheme Study

An analogous warm palette — lemon yellow, orange, red-orange and crimson
— applied to a tessellation of hexagonal blocks set at different heights on a
black base. Yellows are scattered so the eye travels across the whole panel,
and three open cells reveal the black ground as accent points.
